note: Stated choices, one table (docs/coding-principles.md: centralize; prefer data over code). Read only through core.policy.value. A noise tolerance is never here: it is a measured uncertainty (targets.uncertainty) or not checked.

equal_speed_pct.reason: a whole-workload change within this many percent counts as equal speed: not a win and not a regression

tier_a_min_pct.reason: a gain of at least this many percent is a broad win, promotable by default when the guardrails pass

tier_b_min_pct.reason: a gain of at least this many percent is a residual win, promotable with clean rollback and no protected regression

protected_regression_max_pct.reason: a protected context that slows by more than this many percent fails the guardrail

cache_tier_plateau_share.reason: sweep points within this share of their run's median are one cache tier; a step to the next tier is larger

dram_full_read_share.reason: a role whose DRAM bytes are within this share of its weight bytes counts as reading its weights from DRAM

operations_order_ratio.reason: two rows on one input template whose work per launch differs by at least this ratio are told apart by time: the larger takes the slower launches when their measured times do not overlap

same_row_work_ratio.reason: input-side rows of one format whose work per launch is within this ratio are reported as one row

noisy_spread_pct.reason: a timed row whose samples spread more than this many percent (half of P90 - P10 over the median) is labelled noisy

noisy_floor_multiple.reason: a kernel whose median is under this multiple of the dispatch floor is mostly floor: sampled more and labelled noisy

at_ceiling_pct.reason: a kernel at or above this percent of its roofline is called at the ceiling

headroom_pct.reason: a kernel from this percent up to at_ceiling_pct is called moderate headroom; below it, large headroom

mostly_zero_share.reason: an output with at least this share of zeros is called mostly zero

low_correlation.reason: an output whose correlation with the reference is below this is called low correlation

gpu_busy_pct.reason: an Apple GPU whose lowest utilization read is at least this percent is in use by another program (the desktop alone reads 0 to 15)

engine_latest_max_age_h.reason: a look at an engine's upstream releases older than this many hours cannot say a run's build was the latest at run time (engine_builds.currency); llama.cpp publishes several builds a day

update_check_hours.reason: the screen asks the public mirror for a newer BoltBeam at most once in this many hours (cli/self_update.py); a failed check is tried again at the next start

update_check_timeout_s.reason: a look at the mirror's tags that takes longer than this many seconds is a failed check, never up to date

fetch_ssh_connect_timeout_s.reason: boltbeam fetch gives up on a remote that has not answered ssh in this many seconds (BatchMode: it never waits at a prompt)

pairing_max_fused.reason: calls one launch may serve in the pairing (gate and up fused: 2); the pairing rule names it (collectors/pairing.py MAX_FUSED)

pairing_max_split.reason: launches one call may take in the pairing (a library that cuts a product along M); the pairing rule names it (collectors/pairing.py MAX_SPLIT)

pairing_max_nodes.reason: the layer walk stops after this many nodes and says the pairing is unresolved, search_limit (collectors/pairing.py MAX_NODES)

pairing_max_launch_visits.reason: the layer walk stops after visiting this many launches, search_limit: bounds search work as well as nodes on long captures (collectors/pairing.py MAX_LAUNCH_VISITS)

pairing_max_sum_steps.reason: subsets one row's choice may visit in the pairing (collectors/pairing.py MAX_SUM_STEPS)

pairing_inner_spread.reason: two slots' launch times are apart when their inner spreads, this share cut from each end of each slot's sorted launch times, do not overlap: the M = 1 bytes order (collectors/pairing.py SPREAD)

pairing_recurring_share.reason: a slot's kernel runs in at least this share of a kind's layers in a unit, or of the units' last layers (collectors/pairing.py RECUR)

prefill_max_capture_launches.reason: a prefill capture estimated to hold more launches than this is not taken: its untraced time, MFU and clock stand alone (collectors/prefill.py MAX_CAPTURE_LAUNCHES)

replay_max_overhead.reason: the capture-overhead ceiling: a profiled token may run at most this share over the native one; the 5% rule the tie-out and the replay qualification share (collectors/replay_overhead.py MAX_OVERHEAD)

replica_large_row_share.reason: a kernel row of at least this share of the kernel time is a large row for the replication rule (workflow/tie_out.py REPLICA_TOL)

replica_large_row_pct.reason: a run's repeats agree when every large row is within this many percent (workflow/tie_out.py REPLICA_TOL)

replica_any_row_pct.reason: and every other row within this many percent (workflow/tie_out.py REPLICA_TOL)

gemm_prune_ratio.reason: GEMM configs the model puts beyond this ratio of its best are pruned: measured winners sit up to 5.3x above the model's floor, and every cuBLAS pick within 2x (search/gemm_strategy.py PRUNE_RATIO)

prefill_ubatch_min.reason: the smallest prompt chunk (llama.cpp -ub) the prefill setup for experts in RAM considers: llama.cpp's default (workflow/offload.prefill_plan)

prefill_ubatch_max.reason: the largest prompt chunk the prefill setup considers: the compute buffer a chunk needs is not in the fit, and the audit's best chunk with the model in VRAM was 2048 (docs/evidence/strata-audit-20261111)

prefill_ubatch_tie_pct.reason: the prefill setup takes the smallest chunk whose prompt limit is within this many percent of the best one's: a larger chunk costs compute-buffer memory for less than that
